Question
========


```{r logic-df}


logic_type_set1 <- c("$\\exists$", "$\\forall$", "$\\neg \\exists$")
# replace "exists" operator for "not all" operator:
logic_type_set2 <- c("$\\neg \\forall$", "$\\forall$", "$\\neg \\exists$")

# sometimes use "exists", and sometimes "not all":
logic_set_flag <- sample(c(1,2), 1)

logic_df <-
  tibble(
    logic_type_set = c("any", "all", "none"),
    logic_type_symbol = ifelse(logic_set_flag == 1, logic_type_set1, logic_type_set2)
  )




logic_df_sample <- 
  logic_df %>% 
  sample_n(size = 1)

```




```{r random-x-y}
xy_df <-
  tibble(
        x = rnorm(5) %>% round(1),
        y = (rnorm(5)-1.2) %>% round(1)
  )


x <- xy_df$x
y <- xy_df$y

```



Gegeben seien die Mengen $X$ und $Y$ mit jeweils folgenden $n=`r nrow(xy_df)`$ Elementen:


`X={`r  xy_df$x`}`

`Y={`r  xy_df$y`}`


```{r compute-itemlist}

itemlist <- 
  xy_df %>% 
  summarise(
    any_x_lt_y_sol = any(x < y),
    all_x_lt_y_sol = all(x < y),
    none_x_lt_y_sol = !any(x < y),
    any_x_ge_y_sol = any(x >= y),
    all_x_ge_y_sol = all(x >= y),
    none_x_ge_y_sol = !any(x >= y)
    ) %>% 
  pivot_longer(everything(),
               names_to = "logic_type",
               values_to = "is_correct") %>% 
  mutate(proposition_tex = c(
    "$\\exists x[x < y])$ ",
    "$\\forall x[x < y])$",
    "$\\neg \\exists x[x < y])$ ",
    "$\\exists x[x \\ge y])$",
    "$\\forall x[x \\ge y])$",
    "$\\neg \\exists x[x \\ge y])$"
    )) %>% 
  mutate(is_incorrect = !is_correct) %>% 
  pivot_longer(-c(logic_type, proposition_tex),
              names_to = "sol_type",
              values_to = "sol_lgl") %>% 
  sample_n(size = nrow(.)) %>%  # shuffle it
  mutate(sol_type_de = ifelse(sol_type=="is_correct", "wahr", "falsch")) %>% 
  mutate(proposition = glue("'{proposition_tex} ist {sol_type_de}.'")) %>% 
  group_by(sol_type) %>% 
  mutate(id = row_number()) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  filter( (id == 1 & sol_type == "is_correct") | (between(id, 1, 4) & sol_type == "is_incorrect"))

#knitr::kable(itemlist)
```


*Hinweis*: $\neg A$ steht für Negation der Aussage $A$, also das (logische) Gegenteil von $A$.







Wählen Sie die korrekte Aussage aus!


```{r itemlist, results="asis"}
answerlist(itemlist$proposition, markup = "markdown")
```






Solution
========

```{r sol}
sol <- itemlist$proposition[itemlist$sol_type=="is_correct"]
```


Die richtige Aussage lautet "`r sol`".



```{r itemlist_answer, results="asis"}
answerlist(ifelse(itemlist$sol_type=="is_correct", "Wahr", "Falsch"), markup = "markdown")
```
